summary: Typosquat of ethers.js exfiltrates SSH keys, npm/git credentials, browser profiles, and wallet data at install time
details: @wethenorth12/etherjs impersonates the ethers.js library (name 'etherjs', author 'ricmoo', homepage pointing to github.com/ricmoo/etherjs). Its postinstall.js runs automatically on npm install and harvests installer secrets: it enumerates ~/.ssh, reads ~/.npmrc and ~/.gitconfig, inspects Chrome/Firefox/Chromium profiles (Login Data, Cookies), and scans for wallet directories (.bitcoin,.ethereum,.solana,.metamask,.exodus,.electrum). It also captures host identity (hostname, user, npm whoami, git email) and secret-shaped environment variables including NPM_TOKEN, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY, MNEMONIC, and SEED_PHRASE. The collected profile is transmitted via GET to api.telegram.org using a hardcoded bot token and chat_id 8969499041, and POSTed as backup to a serveousercontent.com tunnel at path /collect, with a randomized setTimeout jitter.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
